newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jordan's prime minister slams Netanyahu.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's prime minister slams Netanyahu.

text.p: Jordan's prime minister, in an interview published on Sunday, accused Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu of double talk in Middle East peacemaking.

"We are more than puzzled, we are very much frustrated that what you hear is something and what you see on the ground is something else," Prime Minister Abdel-Karim al-Kabariti told the Israeli newspaper Maariv.

Jordan, partner to a 1994 peace treaty with Israel, had urged Arab states to give the right-wing Netanyahu a chance after his election as prime minister in May. But Kabariti said Jordan was confused by Israel's inconsistencies.
His criticism, the strongest by Jordan yet, echoed remarks by Arab states less friendly to Israel.

"We wanted very much to trust Bibi Netanyahu. We gave Bibi Netanyahu every single chance and we gave him the benefit of the doubt, and we went to the Arab summit meeting and we worked towards convincing everybody that this newly elected prime minister needs time to get his act together," Kabariti said.

Kabariti said Netanyahu told Jordanian officials before his election that his Likud Party would make peace with Arabs in the same way it did with Egypt, which in 1979 became the first Arab state to sign a treaty with Israel.
"So we thought he had it all worked out in his mind, and he has his strategy. Now the question is, 'Does Bibi Netanyahu have a strategy or not?' I don't know," the Jordanian premier said.
He said Jordan has seen "too much inconsistency coming out from Israel. No one can make up their mind on what Israel now wants or is hoping for."
Netanyahu's policy of enlarging Jewish West Bank settlements and delays in handing over parts of Hebron to Palestinian self-rule have raised doubts in the Arab world about his commitment to peace.
Netanyahu opposes swapping land for peace, a cornerstone of five years of negotiations with the Arabs.

His actions have embarrassed Jordan, which for decades has had good, albeit secret, relations with Israel. Relations with Egypt have deteriorated under Netanyahu, and peace talks with Syria are stuck.

Kabariti criticised Netanyahu's decision last September to open a tourist tunnel in Jerusalem near al-Aqsa mosque, Islam's third holiest shrine. The ensuing violence claimed the lives of 60 Palestinians and 15 Israelis.
"For Bibi Netanyahu to take the decision and travel to Europe either shows he lacks the sensitivity towards such issues or he lacks the experience...," Kabariti said.
"It was a big mistake and a mistake that was paid for dearly on the Palestinian side, on the Israeli side and on the peace camp in general."
